1\. drawfn/core/spec.md outside .conduct 📘 Rule violation ⚙ Maintainability 
The PR updates a spec artifact at drawfn/core/SPEC.md, but artifacts like specs must be stored
under drawfn/.conduct/ (or _conduct/ at root) for consistent discovery. Keeping specs outside
the required folders violates the repository artifact-location policy.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description A spec artifact (`drawfn/core/SPEC.md`) is being maintained outside the required artifact locations. Specs/audits/plans should live in `drawfn/.conduct/` (function-level) or `_conduct/` (root-level). ## Issue Context This PR updates the spec content in-place, but the file path violates the artifact placement rule. ## Fix Focus Areas - drawfn/core/SPEC.md[205-247] ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

2\. Broken window pointerup forwarding 🐞 Bug ✓ Correctness 
Drawfn.handleWindowPointerUp forwards a PointerEvent via { ...e }, but real DOM PointerEvent
properties are not enumerable so the forwarded object can lose pointerId/clientX/shiftKey,
causing handlePointerUp to early-return and never clear activePointerId or complete the gesture.
This can leave drag/resize/marquee operations stuck when the pointer is released outside the canvas
(exactly the scenario this handler is meant to fix).
Agent Prompt ```` ## Issue description `handleWindowPointerUp` currently calls `this.handlePointerUp({ ...e, target: this.canvas, currentTarget: this.canvas } as PointerEvent)`. Spreading a real `PointerEvent` does **not** reliably copy fields like `pointerId`, `clientX/clientY`, `shiftKey`, etc. This can cause `handlePointerUp` to ignore the forwarded event and never clear `activePointerId` / complete the gesture. ## Issue Context This handler exists specifically to finalize drags when pointer capture fails or when the pointer is released outside the canvas. If the forwarded event drops `pointerId` or modifier keys, tools and the `activePointerId` gate can break. ## Fix Focus Areas - drawfn/core/src/drawfn.ts[1616-1626] ## Suggested fix Replace the object-spread forwarding with a proxy object that explicitly copies the fields Drawfn/tools read (at minimum `pointerId`, `clientX`, `clientY`, `shiftKey`, `ctrlKey`, `metaKey`, `altKey`, `pressure`, `buttons`, `button`, `pointerType`) and sets `target/currentTarget` to the canvas. Example approach: ```ts private handleWindowPointerUp = (e: PointerEvent): void => { if (this.activePointerId === null || e.pointerId !== this.activePointerId) return; const forwarded = { pointerId: e.pointerId, clientX: e.clientX, clientY: e.clientY, pressure: e.pressure, shiftKey: e.shiftKey, altKey: e.altKey, ctrlKey: e.ctrlKey, metaKey: e.metaKey, button: e.button, buttons: e.buttons, pointerType: e.pointerType, target: this.canvas, currentTarget: this.canvas, } as unknown as PointerEvent; this.handlePointerUp(forwarded); }; ``` Optionally also filter `handlePointerMove` by `activePointerId` for consistency, but the critical fix is eliminating `{...e}` on a real DOM event. ```` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve pointerId when proxying window pointerup**

Forwarding the `PointerEvent` with object spread drops non-enumerable event fields (including `pointerId`, coordinates, and modifier keys). In the off-canvas release path this means `handlePointerUp` receives an event with missing `pointerId`, fails the active-pointer guard, and never completes the gesture/historical transaction. Users who release the pointer outside the canvas can end up with a stuck drag/resize state and missing undo snapshot.
